data.content_ref: inline:SRC_001's claim explicitly restricts refusal to 'log corruption from causes other than budget exhaustion,' deliberately excluding budget-caused corruption. Yet its own first countercondition admits that an inaccurate per-event budget estimate can cause mid-write exhaustion, which IS budget-caused log corruption (a partial or torn event at the tail). This creates a direct contradiction: the claim says resumption is 'always safe as long as the log's append-only identity is intact' and only refuses on non-budget corruption, but budget exhaustion itself can produce a partial write that corrupts the append-only identity—a refusal case the claim's stated conditions omit. The problem asks for the cases in which resumption must stay refused; SRC_001 leaves the most directly relevant refusal case (budget-exhaustion-induced partial write) unaddressed by its main conditions.
